<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-docs.mjs from the repository. Do not edit here. -->
This guide takes the GRANDstack repos and turns them into an app for **your own data**. The worked example is a small library: **Books**, **Authors** and **Genres**, with a relationship property on who wrote what. Every step here was run end to end: the Books server answered queries, `codegen` generated types from its schema, and a typed Books page built and rendered.

You will:

1. Describe your data in a GraphQL schema and a seed file.
2. Run the server on it (no code changes, no rebuild).
3. Generate types and build a front end that reads it.

Time: about 20 minutes. You need Docker or Podman with compose, Node 22 or later, and the three repositories (`grandstack`, `grandstack-server`, `grandstack-web`) side by side in one folder.

## Part 1: the server

### 1. Write the schema

Create `grandstack/my-app/schema.graphql`. Rules (details in the server's `docs/schema-guide.md`): every type that is stored in Neo4j needs `@node`, relationships are declared from both sides, and every type and field should have a description.

```graphql
"""A book in the library."""
type Book @node {
  """Book title. Unique."""
  title: String!
  """Year of first publication."""
  published: Int
  """Number of pages."""
  pages: Int
  """Average reader rating from 0 to 5."""
  rating: Float
  """Genres the book belongs to."""
  genres: [Genre!]! @relationship(type: "IN_GENRE", direction: OUT)
  """People who wrote or contributed to the book."""
  authors: [Author!]! @relationship(type: "WROTE", direction: IN, properties: "Wrote")
}

"""A person who wrote books."""
type Author @node {
  """Full name. Unique."""
  name: String!
  """Year of birth."""
  born: Int
  """Books the person wrote."""
  books: [Book!]! @relationship(type: "WROTE", direction: OUT, properties: "Wrote")
}

"""A book genre."""
type Genre @node {
  """Genre name."""
  name: String!
  """Books in this genre."""
  books: [Book!]! @relationship(type: "IN_GENRE", direction: IN)
}

"""Properties on the WROTE relationship."""
type Wrote @relationshipProperties {
  """How the person contributed, for example author or translator."""
  role: String!
}
```

`direction` is relative to the type the field sits on: `Book.authors` is `IN` (the arrow goes from Author to Book), `Author.books` is `OUT` for the same `WROTE` relationship.

### 2. Write the seed

Create `grandstack/my-app/books.cypher`. Statements end with a semicolon at the end of a line, use `MERGE` so reloading is safe, and the first line carries a version.

```cypher
// seed-version: 1
CREATE CONSTRAINT book_title IF NOT EXISTS FOR (b:Book) REQUIRE b.title IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT author_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (a:Author) REQUIRE a.name IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT genre_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (g:Genre) REQUIRE g.name IS UNIQUE;
UNWIND [
  {title: "Dune", published: 1965, pages: 412, rating: 4.3, genres: ["Sci-Fi"], authors: [{name: "Frank Herbert", role: "author"}]},
  {title: "Neuromancer", published: 1984, pages: 271, rating: 3.9, genres: ["Sci-Fi"], authors: [{name: "William Gibson", role: "author"}]},
  {title: "Good Omens", published: 1990, pages: 288, rating: 4.3, genres: ["Fantasy", "Comedy"], authors: [{name: "Terry Pratchett", role: "author"}, {name: "Neil Gaiman", role: "author"}]},
  {title: "The Hobbit", published: 1937, pages: 310, rating: 4.3, genres: ["Fantasy"], authors: [{name: "J. R. R. Tolkien", role: "author"}]},
  {title: "Emma", published: 1815, pages: 474, rating: 4.0, genres: ["Romance"], authors: [{name: "Jane Austen", role: "author"}]}
] AS b
MERGE (book:Book {title: b.title}) SET book.published = b.published, book.pages = b.pages, book.rating = b.rating
FOREACH (g IN b.genres | MERGE (ge:Genre {name: g}) MERGE (book)-[:IN_GENRE]->(ge))
FOREACH (a IN b.authors | MERGE (au:Author {name: a.name}) MERGE (au)-[r:WROTE]->(book) SET r.role = a.role);
```

Map keys in Cypher are bare words (`title:`), not quoted strings.

### 3. Point the server at them

Create `grandstack/compose.books.yaml`. It overrides the `server` service so the image uses your files and settings instead of the Movies ones, with no rebuild:

```yaml
services:
  server:
    environment:
      SEED_PATH: /app/seed/books.cypher   # which seed file to load
      SEED_PROBE_LABEL: Book              # label used to tell whether the database already has data
      REFRESH_COUNTS: "false"             # the Movies sample keeps film counts on Person; you have none
    volumes:
      - ./my-app/schema.graphql:/app/schema/schema.graphql:ro
      - ./my-app/books.cypher:/app/seed/books.cypher:ro
```

### 4. Start Neo4j and the server

Stop the Movies stack first if it is running (it uses the same ports), then start only Neo4j and the server under their own project name so the Movies data is not mixed in:

```sh
cd grandstack
docker compose down
docker compose -p mybooks -f compose.yaml -f compose.books.yaml up --build neo4j server
```

The server log should say `Loaded seed` and `GraphQL ready at http://localhost:4000/graphql`. Open that URL for GraphiQL, or:

```sh
curl -s localhost:4000/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ books(sort:[{rating:DESC}]) { title published authors { name } genres { name } } }"}'
```

### 5. Try writes

Everything the library generates for `Book` works with no more code: filters, sorting, `booksConnection` with `totalCount`, and create, update and delete. This one connects an existing author and creates a new one, setting the relationship property on each:

```graphql
mutation($i: [BookCreateInput!]!) {
  createBooks(input: $i) { books { title authorsConnection { edges { properties { role } node { name } } } } }
}
```
```json
{ "i": [{ "title": "Anathem", "published": 2008,
          "authors": { "connect": [{ "where": { "node": { "name": { "eq": "William Gibson" } } }, "edge": { "role": "translator" } }],
                       "create":  [{ "node": { "name": "Neal Stephenson" }, "edge": { "role": "author" } }] } }] }
```

The rules for updates and deletes, including how to change relationships safely, are in the server's `docs/mutations.md`.

### 6. Change the seed later

Edit `books.cypher` and **bump `// seed-version`**; on the next server start the database reloads it. Without a bump nothing happens. Note: the marker node is named `movies` regardless of your data (an implementation detail, harmless). Check the log for `Loaded seed` or `Seed already loaded, skipping`.

## Part 2: a front end

The web app is written for Movies. Codegen shows exactly what depends on that.

### 7. Copy the web app and see what breaks

```sh
cp -R grandstack-web my-library-web
cd my-library-web
rm -rf node_modules dist && npm ci
npm run codegen
```

With the Books server running, codegen fails with a list like `Cannot query field "movies" on type "Query"` (49 errors for the stock app). That list is every place the app assumes Movies, which is the point: the schema is the contract.

### 8. Keep what is generic, remove what is not

```sh
rm -rf src/pages src/search src/forms src/graph e2e docs
rm src/lib/filters.ts src/lib/filters.test.ts src/lib/peopleFilters.ts src/lib/peopleFilters.test.ts src/lib/compare.tsx
npm pkg delete scripts.e2e scripts.docs:check
```

What stays and is reusable as it is: `src/ui` (buttons, chips, dialog, avatar), `src/poster` (generated posters), `src/theme` and `styles.css`, and `src/lib/hash.ts` and `initials.ts`. See the web repo's `docs/customising.md` for the full table.

### 9. Write a typed page

Create `src/pages/Books.tsx`. The query in `graphql()` is validated against your schema and typed by `codegen`:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { useQuery } from "urql";
import { graphql } from "../graphql/generated";
import { Poster } from "../poster/Poster";
import { RatingBadge } from "../ui";

const BooksQuery = graphql(`
  query Books($search: String!) {
    books(where: { title: { contains: $search } }, sort: [{ rating: DESC }]) {
      title
      published
      pages
      rating
      genres { name }
      authorsConnection {
        edges {
          properties { role }
          node { name }
        }
      }
    }
  }
`);

export function Books() {
  const [search, setSearch] = useState("");
  const [{ data, fetching, error }] = useQuery({ query: BooksQuery, variables: { search } });

  return (
    <section>
      <input className="text-input" placeholder="Search by title (case-sensitive)" value={search}
        onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)} aria-label="Search books" />
      {error && <p className="error">{error.message}</p>}
      {fetching && !data && <p>Loading…</p>}
      <div className="grid" style={{ marginTop: 24 }}>
        {data?.books.map((b) => (
          <article key={b.title} className="card">
            <Poster title={b.title} year={b.published} genre={b.genres[0]?.name} />
            <div className="card-body">
              <div className="card-head">
                <strong className="card-title">{b.title}</strong>
                <RatingBadge rating={b.rating} />
              </div>
              <p className="card-meta">
                {b.authorsConnection.edges.map((e) => `${e.node.name} (${e.properties.role})`).join(", ")}
              </p>
              <p className="card-genres">{b.genres.map((g) => g.name).join(" · ")}{b.pages ? ` · ${b.pages} pages` : ""}</p>
            </div>
          </article>
        ))}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Replace `src/App.tsx` with:

```tsx
import { Books } from "./pages/Books";

export function App() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>My Library</h1>
      <Books />
    </main>
  );
}
```

And replace `src/main.tsx` with this version, which drops the router (you removed every route):

```tsx
import "@fontsource-variable/public-sans";
import { StrictMode } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { MotionConfig } from "motion/react";
import { Client, Provider, cacheExchange, fetchExchange } from "urql";
import { App } from "./App";
import "./theme/tokens.css";
import "./styles.css";

const client = new Client({
  url: import.meta.env.VITE_GRAPHQL_URL ?? "http://localhost:4000/graphql",
  exchanges: [cacheExchange, fetchExchange],
  requestPolicy: "cache-and-network",
});

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <Provider value={client}>
      <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">
        <App />
      </MotionConfig>
    </Provider>
  </StrictMode>,
);
```

### 10. Generate types, check, run

```sh
npm run codegen      # must succeed now: it validates your query against the Books schema
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run dev          # http://localhost:3000
```

You should see six book cards with generated posters, authors with their roles and genres. (The dev server uses port 3000, which the server allows by default through `CORS_ORIGIN`.)

## Where to go next

Use the web repo's `docs/recipes.md` for the patterns, adapted to your entities:

- **Filters in the URL:** copy the idea of `src/lib/filters.ts` (parse, serialize, `buildWhere`) in the original repo for your own fields.
- **Facet counts, people browser, compare, graph views:** see the web repo's `docs/features.md` for how each works.
- **Create, edit, delete forms:** `src/forms/model.ts` in the original repo shows how form state becomes nested mutation inputs and relationship diffs.
- **Computed fields:** add `@cypher` fields like `Movie.similar` (see `docs/schema-guide.md` in `grandstack-server`).
- Keep the server's rules in mind: describe every field, bump the seed version, and update relationships as diffs.

## Adding login to your app

The auth setup in `grandstack-auth` is not tied to Movies. The pieces you would reuse:

- **The gateway** (`gateway/`) is generic: point `UPSTREAM_URL` at your server, set the issuer, audience and JWKS URL, and list your mutations in `MUTATION_PERMISSIONS` in `gateway/rules.ts` with the permission each needs (unknown mutations are refused).
- **Row-level rules** live in an extra schema file for your own types (see `schema/auth.graphql` for `filter` rules, `$jwt.sub` comparisons and the "author comes from the token" pattern). The server loads it with `SCHEMA_EXTRA_PATHS` and verifies tokens when the three `AUTH_*` variables are set. Mind the v7 pitfalls: `validate` rules and `DateTime` need APOC.
- **Roles and users** come from your identity provider; the dev realm file shows the Keycloak side, and `docs/swapping-providers.md` lists what to change for another provider.
- **A front end** needs an OpenID Connect client; `grandstack-auth/docs/exercise-add-auth-to-grandstack-web.md` walks through it.

## What is Movies-specific and what is not

| Reusable as is | Pattern to copy | Movies-specific |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The server image, config, plugin mechanism, seed versioning, `src/ui`, posters, theme, graph view component | URL-synced filters, facet counts, diff-based update inputs, typed operations | `schema/schema.graphql`, `seed/movies.cypher`, `src/pages`, `src/search`, the people and movie filters |
